Surreal Business Lunch Experience
Nov 2017 • Business
I had come here once at night, the place is a nice well lit rooftop restaurant with average Vietnamese food, was so-so ok.
Yesterday, I went there for a business lunch. By no means would I ever use this channel to put anyone’s business down, but I hope service improves if harsh words are listened to. Also, it was a business lunch.
Not only the staff was unprepared for foreign costumers, the food we had was disgraceful, with hair on the braised pork and a watery purple yum soup with chicken bones floating around amidst undercooked lotus roots.
The best of the 1-hour lunch meeting: watching a family of 5-6 rats playing 2-meters away from me outside in the plants in broad daylight to the staff’s complete indifference.
I am quite flexible this is Vietnam, but if I want to take risks of things being like this I’d just eat out on the street for a lot less. This shouldn’t pass unnoticed. Hope they seriously improve in he future. Service zero, food zero, rat entertainment 10/10.

A 5-star restaurant you must try
Jan 2017 • Friends
My girlfriend and I met a new Vietnamese friend, and on her suggestion, we dined here last night. It was her first time to eat here as well, but she knew of the chef (minor chef celeb in HCMC) and thought it would be a good choice.

It was an EXCELLENT choice. From the funky decor, rooftop location, to the relaxing, simple but elegant ambience, we knew without even seeing the menu this would be a great meal.

Started with an excellent pineapple juice (from a variety of fresh juices), and then we made three choices: grilled chicken, white eggplant and stuffed tofu. They were all prepared beautifully and each had a memorable taste. I'm a bit of a tofu aficionado (OK, a tofu snob), and I'd never eaten stuffed tofu so the veggie fillings and grilling in a fermented tofu sauce was a first - excellent and worthy of my experimenting to try to duplicate it.

The eggplant was cooked lightly in some kind of oil, just right, and had a light sweet taste. My girlfriend raved about the chicken. 

Then on to the desserts. We tried something with artichoke (for dessert?? YES!) and although I'm not sure what was in it, it was superb. We also tried the caramelized banana and another banana/ice cream combination. Each was a new but wonderful taste treat.

Finished off with a wonderful whipped cream coffee, which topped everything off - and another wonderful taste experience.

All in all, this place is a must-try. In 12 months, I'm sure it will have loads of 5-star reviews. As we were leaving, the owner (a very kind, gentle man) asked us how everything was and told us a bit about his goal of serving authentic, natural foods, in typical Vietnamese style. Believe me, he succeeded! And all three of us ate sumptuously for an unbelievably cheap price of $25.
